title: Micro-slab metrics quicksheet — Maya
body:
Purpose:
Quick, personal tracking sheet for micro-slab runs — keep a compact log of short experiments (10–60s each) so I can spot regressions and rough cost/latency tradeoffs without firing up the full bench dashboard. Not authoritative; notes-to-self style.

Context / hypothesis:
- Trying small KV-cache enabled prefix caching across model variants to see p95 behavior under 8k seq.
- Expectation: enabling prefix cache + slab batching reduces p95 by ~15–30% for short bursts at cost of slightly higher p50 variance due to batching.
- Primary metrics: tokens/s (throughput), p50 ms, p95 ms, cost per 1k tokens (approx), and stray failures.

Run table (most recent at top):
ID | t | model | variant | batch | kv_cache | seq_len | tokens/s | p50_ms | p95_ms | errors | est_cost_per_1k | notes
----|---|-------|---------|-------|----------|--------|----------|--------|--------|--------|------------------|------
run-20240914-09 | 09:02 | gptx-3.8b | fp16 | 4 | on | 2048 | 1420 | 88 | 240 | 0 | $0.52 | warm KV cache, steady tokens/s
run-20240914-08 | 08:40 | gptx-3.8b | int8-q | 8 | off | 1024 | 1180 | 76 | 310 | 1 | $0.23 | one timeout on tail, p95 spike
run-20240913-17 | 17:15 | gptx-3.8b | fp16 | 2 | on | 4096 | 960 | 110 | 390 | 0 | $0.60 | long prefix — cache shows benefit on p50
run-20240913-11 | 11:03 | gptx-3.8b | int8-q | 16 | on | 512 | 2350 | 40 | 120 | 0 | $0.15 | high throughput, low p95 with small seq

Quick notes / observations:
- int8-q + small batches (8–16) gives best tokens/s on short sequences but p95 can vary if cache misses happen.
- fp16 tends to have more stable p95 but higher cost per token.
- On runs where I saw an isolated error, it was usually a transient OOM on the node (tracked in slack thread). Will add an explicit retry in bench harness.

Checklist (next actions):
- [ ] Add an automated retry loop for transient node OOMs (ticket PROJ-219).
- [ ] Re-run the 8k seq experiments with forced cold KV-cache to get baseline cold hits (2 runs per variant).
- [ ] Export top-5 runs to bench CSV and upload to shared bench dashboard for trend analysis.
- [ ] Note any model-architecture differences (attn kernel selects) in the run metadata.

Questions / TODOs for pairing with Rhea/Ethan:
- Are we confident the est_cost_per_1k matches the new pricing formula used by the billing team? (cc billing on PR)
- Follow up: should we consider a hybrid policy that routes small seq to int8-q and long seq to fp16? Quick sim needed.

Short command snippets I keep forgetting:
- Run quick micro-slab locally (dev harness):
  ./bench --variant int8-q --batch 8 --seq 512 --warm-cache 1 --label quicktest
- Extract tokens/s and p95 via jq from bench JSON:
  jq '.summary | {tps: .tokens_per_sec, p95: .p95_ms}' out.json

Links (for myself):
- PR with bench harness tweaks: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/742
- Jira: PROJ-219 (retry + OOM handling)
- Slack thread where a node flaked: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C02ABC123/p1670000000000000
- Confluence scratch doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/Micro+slab+experiments

Sticky notes / brain dump (messy):
- If cache warming is the main variance source, we should record cache-hit ratio per run in the bench JSON (I keep forgetting to enable it).
- Might be worth a tiny canary that runs every hour on dedicated pool A to see if p95 drifts overnight.
- Keep this mini-sheet trimmed — move stable summaries to shared bench dashboard.

End of sheet.
(Short lived; will iterate — probably rename to "micro-slab-weekly-snap" if it becomes a weekly artifact.)
